learning_outcomes.text: Assimilation of notions and vocabulary of automatics, system modeling, principles and structure of automatic systems, execution and measurement elements, stages of designing automatic control systems and finite-state systems.
Creation of competences in modeling, operating with Matlab analysis and simulation environment, operating and programming programmable logic controllers.
Recognition, understanding, and explanation of simple automatic system structures.
Definition of basic concepts, theories, and methods in the fundamental domain of engineering sciences; their adequate use in professional communication.
Association of mechanical domain structures with component parts of automatic systems.
Analysis of fundamental system properties (stability) in both time and frequency domains.
Elementary operation with Matlab analysis and design environment and with programmable logic controller programming environment.

syllabus_topics: Systems: Introductory notions regarding the concept of system and automatic system, with examples, and analysis through examples
Introduction. Definitions
Automatic system. Examples. Operation. Comparison with human-operated systems
Automatic control systems: Detailing the concept of automatic control system (ACS), types of ACS, stages of ACS design
Conventional Automatic Control System (CACS). Description, operation
Structures derived from CACS
Stages of ACS design
Mathematical models in time, MM-II, MM-ISI and in operational form, transfer function
Quality indicators of ACS
Measurement and execution elements
Regulator design, structure, algorithms
Elements of ACS analysis. Time and frequency domain analysis. Stability
Implementation of regulators. Technologies for automatic regulator realization. Commissioning
Finite-state systems: Presentation of automatic finite-state systems, modeling, control
Concept of finite-state system. Examples. Modeling
Control elements for finite-state systems
Programmable logic controller. Structure, programming
Mobile robots: History, Geometry of robots, Notions of motion and localization, Notions of positioning, control of autonomous mobile robots
Equipment used
Modeling of automatic control systems: Examples of mechanical, thermal, electrical systems. Modeling based on structure and physical operating equations
Simulation of mechanical processes: Time analysis of mechanical, thermal systems. Simulation. Use of MATLAB+Simulink design environment in system analysis
Process control: Analysis of control systems regarding setpoint and disturbance changes. Stability, control quality
Discrete event systems: Modeling of discrete event systems. Introduction to programmable logic controller. Writing programs for process control
assessment_rules: The course grade is based on a written exam (66%) covering basic notions and understanding of automatic systems structures and mechanisms. The applied activities grade (34%) is based on questions, tests, observation of active participation, and answers to questions. Minimum performance standards are presented for passing the discipline.
